data.title: The Content Cud Problem
paragraphs: Your customer shouldn't be the first person to read your content.

People have edited each other's writing for centuries. AI made it easy to skip that step, and most agencies and tools now do. They publish hundreds of pages and no one ever reads a word, so your brand ends up sounding like the billion other brands that Claude or Gemini or ChatGPT or whatever LLM already scraped.
So who would read it? If you are regurgitating content cud like a cow, who else is going to read it?

We keep a person in the loop. We capture your voice first, then someone reads every page before it ships. We rewrote about 100 articles end to end to prove it holds at volume, and even with a tight spec about a third came back short and a couple had the wrong content attached before a person caught it. That is what slips when nobody reads. The discipline is old. Doing it at AI scale is the part most shops drop.

data.title: Houston, you have a problem
data.subtitle: If one of these sounds like your site, a content refresh is the move.

items.title: A back catalog dragging you down
items.text: Hundreds of old posts that are out of date, off-brand, or thin. They still rank, still get crawled, and still shape what people and AI think of you.

items.title: A platform migration
items.text: You are moving CMS or merging sites and everything needs to come across rewritten from scratch. A migration is the moment to fix the content while everything is already open.

items.title: A voice that drifted
items.text: Years of different writers and agencies left your content sounding like ten brands. You want one voice across every page, old and new.

items.title: Invisible to AI search
items.text: Your pages were written for a different web. They are not structured for AI engines to read, quote, and cite, so you are missing from the answers buyers see first.

items.title: You sound like everyone else
items.text: Your content reads like the same scrape every competitor published. A reader has no reason to stay, and an AI engine has no reason to cite you over anyone else.

items.title: Facts that went stale
items.text: Old stats, dead links, discontinued products, and last year's pricing are quietly eroding trust on pages you forgot you had.

items.title: Rankings slipping for no obvious reason
items.text: Pages that used to rank are sliding. The web moved, competitors refreshed, and your content went quiet. That is content decay, and it keeps getting worse.

items.title: More pages than your team can fix by hand
items.text: You know the library needs work. Refreshing hundreds of pages one at a time never reaches the top of anyone's list, so it never gets done.

data.title: The engine is RequestDesk
data.subtitle: Voice capture and quality control run as a system you can see, step by step.

steps.title: Capture your voice
steps.text: RequestDesk studies your existing content and builds a voice profile. It captures tone, rhythm, reading level, and what you do and do not say. We refine it with you and lock it as the standard.

steps.title: Encode your brand rules
steps.text: Banned phrases, required spellings, competitors you never link. We load them into RequestDesk so the rules are enforced on every page automatically.

steps.title: Ground it in your content
steps.text: We index your current pages and source documents so each rewrite draws on your own facts. This is the layer that keeps the work grounded.

steps.title: Rewrite and encode at scale
steps.text: Each page is rewritten to your voice and structured for AI search, with a clear answer up front, descriptive headings, internal and authority links, and an FAQ block.

steps.title: QA-gate every piece
steps.text: Nothing ships until it passes the gate for voice match, fact accuracy, brand rules, and AEO structure. Whatever fails gets reworked before it ships.

data.title: Inside every page we touch
data.subtitle: Each page of your content goes through the same six steps. No skimming, no copy-paste.

items.title: Read and ground in the original
items.text: We read your existing page in full and pull the facts that matter, so the rewrite builds on what is true about your business.

items.title: Rewrite to your captured voice
items.text: A writer rebuilds the page against your locked voice profile, matching tone, rhythm, reading level, and the words you do and do not use.

items.title: Structure for AI search
items.text: The answer goes up front, with a primary question in the headline, descriptive subheads, and an FAQ block, so AI engines can read and cite it.

items.title: Add internal and authority links
items.text: Descriptive links to your own pages and to credible outside sources. Never a competitor, never a filler anchor like click here.

items.title: Fact-check against your material
items.text: Every claim is checked against your source content. Outdated stats get refreshed. Anything we cannot verify gets flagged for your review.

items.title: Run the QA gate
items.text: The page must pass voice match, accuracy, brand rules, and structure before it counts as done. Whatever fails goes back for rework.

data.title: You pay for the result, not the clock
paragraphs: You are buying the finished work. Every page rewritten in your voice, structured for AI search, fact-checked, and QA-passed. We quote one project price for that result, and you approve the number before we start. It does not move with our timesheet.

So why show the hours at all? Because the work behind every page is substantial, and we want you to see it. A person reads every word at a heavy-edit standard, roughly 1,000 words for every 15 to 20 minutes of careful reading, fact-checking, and voice and structure correction, plus a one-time two to three hours to capture your voice. We show that depth so the price is never a black box. The hours shape the scope of the quote.

A recent full refresh ran about 100 articles and 140,000 words, dozens of hours of human review, delivered as one outcome. What you buy is content that earns its place in AI search. Behind the platform sits a team with 30 years in ecommerce content and a bench of professional writers.

items.question: Will the rewrites sound like us?
items.answer: Yes. We do not start writing until we have captured your voice into a profile and confirmed it with you. From there, every page is graded against that profile, so all your content reads like one brand.

items.question: Do you make up facts about our business?
items.answer: No. We index your existing content and any source material you give us, and the rewrites draw from that. If something is not in your material, we flag it for you.

items.question: What is AEO and why does it matter?
items.answer: AEO is structuring content so AI search engines can read it, quote it, and cite you as the source. Buyers increasingly get answers from AI before they ever reach a search results page. If your pages are not built for that, you are absent from the answer.

items.question: If you do not charge by the hour, why show the hours?
items.answer: Because the work behind every page is substantial, and we want it visible. This is not a cheap content dump. We show the human review behind every page, roughly 1,000 words for every 15 to 20 minutes of careful reading, fact-checking, and correction, so you can see the depth you are paying for. The hours tell us how to size your project. They do not set your bill.

items.question: How long does a full refresh take?
items.answer: It depends on the page count and how much grounding material exists. We run the work in controlled batches so quality holds at volume, and you get a delivery timeline alongside the quote. A recent refresh of about 100 articles moved through in a matter of weeks.

items.question: Do you publish the pages or only write them?
items.answer: Either. We can deliver clean, formatted drafts for your team to review and publish, or push approved pages straight to your CMS. You decide where the handoff is.

items.question: How is it priced?
items.answer: By the outcome, not the hour. We quote one fixed project price for the finished work, every page rewritten, AEO-structured, fact-checked, and QA-passed. You approve that number before we start, and it does not change based on how long the work takes us. Request a scope above and we will price your project.
